Autumn is a major season for sports fans, and ESPN has recently rolled out a significant upgrade for users of its tvOS and iOS apps: 4K HDR streaming playback.

ESPN's streaming service now supports 4K HDR, with the tvOS and iOS apps being the first to add support

Over the past few weeks, ESPN has begun rolling out a major upgrade in its tvOS and iOS apps.

The streaming service now offers 4K HDR picture quality for top-tier programming, including live events from the NFL, NBA, NHL, and more.

This week, ESPN and ESPN2 will begin broadcasting in 4K HDR in the United States, enhancing picture quality for fans during the most-watched stretch of the sports calendar all year. This includes all Monday Night Football, NBA, and NHL games produced by ESPN, as well as select live college football and US Open tennis events, plus marquee events like Super Bowl LXI. The update will bring sharper edges, more vivid colours, and smoother motion — all critical to delivering a richer, more immersive viewing experience for sports fans. The ESPN app on iOS and tvOS will be the first to support the new experience, with other connected TV platforms to follow, and ESPN Unlimited subscribers on Disney+ in the United States will also have access.

While browsing the ESPN app, you'll notice a new "4K HDR" label on content that supports higher-quality streaming.

As long as you have a stable internet connection at home or on the go, 4K HDR can deliver more vivid, clearer, and higher-quality visuals for your favourite sports content.

If any sports fans are tempted to pick up an Apple TV 4K for the first time, we'd suggest holding off for a bit. Reports indicate that the wait for an all-new Apple TV model is nearly over.

Since ESPN launched its 4K HDR content, have you watched any of it? How does it look? Drop us a note in the comments section.
